 Real Madrid Thrash Leipzig to Maintain Perfect Champions League Record
 By David Egbede 1 min read RELATED Champions League: United Hit 4, Bayern Smash 5 as Como Shock Leipzig Real Madrid Sign Yan Diomandé from Leipzig for €140m EXCLUSIVE: Yan Diomande Flies to Madrid Ahead of Real Madrid Move Real Madrid Agree Five-Year Deal With Yan Diomande Declan Rice Rescues Arsenal as Gunners Hold Bayern Munich to Draw Real Madrid continued their impressive start to the UEFA Champions League with a convincing 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday, securing their third win in three matches.
 Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande were on target for Jose Mourinho’s side as the Spanish giants extended their winning run across all competitions to four matches.
 Madrid broke the deadlock towards the end of a closely contested first half when Silva reacted quickest to a rebound and scored from close range. It was the midfielder’s first goal since joining the club this summer.
 Guler doubled Madrid’s advantage in the 52nd minute after connecting with a move involving Jude Bellingham and Mbappe. The Turkish midfielder held off a defender before turning the ball into the net.
 Mbappe added a third with a curling finish after being set up by Diomande, who had come on as a substitute for Vinicius Junior with 20 minutes remaining.
 Advertisement Ad Feedback RELATED Champions League: United Hit 4, Bayern Smash 5 as Como Shock Leipzig Leipzig briefly reduced the deficit when Tidiam Gomis capitalised on a defensive lapse by Dean Huijsen to beat goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois.
 However, Diomande restored Madrid’s three-goal cushion with a spectacular volley into the top corner from Brahim Diaz’s cross, sealing an emphatic victory.
 Leipzig had threatened early in the match, but Courtois produced an excellent save to deny Romulo Cardoso. Madrid gradually took control, with goalkeeper Maarten Vandevoordt making several saves before the Spanish side eventually broke through.
 Mourinho’s team will take confidence from the result as they prepare for Sunday’s LaLiga Clasico against arch-rivals Barcelona.
 Despite enduring an inconsistent domestic start and going two seasons without a major trophy, Madrid have maintained a perfect record in Europe this campaign.
 Their victory also provides a positive response following Barcelona’s defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday, as the race for Champions League supremacy intensifies.
